messages.subject: telemetry, captured and sightings
parts:
I’m fitting a somewhat unconventional SECR model, and was wondering if I could get some advice. Sorry if this is really long, it’s my first time asking for this kind of advice.

 

Study Description:

14 animals were live-captured and GPS collared over the course of 7 months.
Collars were fitted with unique visual markers.
After capture/marking was complete, animals were exposed for 2 months to 3 types of devices.
Devices were deactivated to prevent animal capture (to protect the GPS collar) but ‘captures’ were recorded via camera monitoring: this can be approximated as resighting data.

 The primary aim of the study is to calculate sigma and capture probability. Density is secondary.

 

Modelling approach:

I’m using SECR 4.5.4. So far I’ve modelled this data as a resighting study, using camera observations. However, I know my marked animals are clustered, and I think I need to include their known distribution.

I know I can do this using the mark-recapture data. However, I’ve been avoiding that because 1) I have hundreds of capture nights spread across chaotic field notes, and traps were shifted regularly. I could address the shifting using usage but it would still be laborious and potentially a little inaccurate. 2) The capture/marking period was so long (~7 months) that I very much doubt it was a closed system.

I was thinking I could instead use the GPS data, and this might have the additional benefit of improving sigma and g0 estimates. However, it appears GPS data is not compatible with mark-resight (https://www.otago.ac.nz/density/pdfs/secr-telemetry.pdf) at least in secr 4.5. The info file mentions the caveat “except possibly in distinct sessions (this has not been tested)”, but I’m not sure exactly what this means: does this refer to when you are modelling only 1 session?


So I guess I’ve got three questions:

1)     Given I am primarily aiming for calculating sigma and g0, and density is secondary, I think having the known distribution of marked animals is more important than avoiding violating the closed-system assumption. I’m not a statistician. Does that sound reasonable?

2)     Is GPS data still incompatible with resighting data in 4.5.4? I am only modelling one session, does that change things?

3)     Is there any other way I could use the GPS data or simplify the capture/recapture data to add the known distribution of individuals? E.g. using sigmas and home range centres calculated from GPS data?


Thank you for your help!
